subject: Re: Flikweert Vision + Encord
text:
Hi Arisha,

Since Encord will be introducing multi-stage / stage specific labeling in Q1 2026, we’d like to confirm whether our proposed workflow below aligns with what will be possible once multi-stage is released.

Proposal: two-stage annotation with targeted consensus on positive samples
Stage 1 annotation (all images)

  *
Annotators perform a coarse classification to decide whether a defect is present.
     *
defect ? routed to stage 2
     *
not-defect ? completed as not-defect
     *
skip ? completed as skip
     *
doubt ? completed as doubt

Stage 2 annotation (defect images only)

  *
Only images labeled as “defect” in stage 1 are reviewed again to determine the defect type.
     *
subdefect 1 ? completed as subdefect 1
     *
subdefect 2 ? completed as subdefect 2
     *
subdefect 3 ? completed as subdefect 3
     *
not-defect ? completed as doubt (no consensus)
     *
skip ? completed as doubt (no consensus)
     *
doubt ? completed as doubt (no consensus)

Why we would like to do this

  *
In stage 1, annotators only decide if the defect is present or not, which reduces complexity.
  *
In stage 2, annotators can focus on identifying the correct sub-defect type (e.g. small vs. severe damage), while also providing a second review of defect cases.
  *
Consensus is only applied on where it matters (defect images). This avoids spending time applying consensus to low-value cases like “skip”.
  *
We don’t apply consensus on the subdefects.
  *
We avoid missing “not-defect” images with unnecessary consensus. From experience, fewer errors occur on the “not-defect” label. We therefore do not apply consensus here initially, but can evaluate later whether consensus provides additional benefit.

Additional context:

  *
We assume that different annotators will annotate the same image in stage 2. Either by enforcing this on image level (annotators may work on both stages, but never on the same image twice) or stage level (different annotators for different stages).

subject: Re: Encord - Interest
text:
Hi Hugo,

My interest in Encord stems from its strong alignment with my work in AI
systems for high-risk governance environments and production workflows. I
build and advise on AI solutions where data quality, traceability,
auditability, and human-in-the-loop oversight are critical, especially in
regulated, government-adjacent, and safety-critical contexts. Encord's
focus on dataset curation, annotation, model evaluation, and governance
directly addresses the challenges I face in creating trustworthy AI and
compliance-ready pipelines.

Our team is a small, cross-functional group of 2-5 senior members covering
AI/ML engineering, data automation, and governance. We operate leanly and
scale contributors as projects progress.

Currently, our projects are in the early-to-mid build stage, transitioning
from proof-of-concept to structured pilots. We are focused on validating
data pipelines and governance controls over the next 3-6 months, with a
goal to scale operations within 6-12 months.

Warm regards,
